title: Flat pullback preserves schematic density of quasi-compact open subspaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Morphism properties use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]; locally finite type is the chart test with [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be flat. Let $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion, meaning a representable open subspace inclusion [def-a1-space-open-subspace] which is quasi-compact, meaning its inverse image on every affine etale scheme chart is quasi-compact. Suppose $\mathcal O_Y\to j_*\mathcal O_V$ is injective as sheaves on the small etale site. Then $j_X:X\times_YV\hookrightarrow X$ is again a quasi-compact open immersion, and $\mathcal O_X\to (j_X)_*\mathcal O_{X\times_YV}$ is injective. Thus $X\times_YV$ is schematically dense in $X$.

source.place: Tag 089D (lemma-flat-morphism-scheme-theoretically-dense-open); quasi-compactness and openness are preserved by base change on scheme tests.

proof.text: Choose a scheme atlas $p:Y_0\to Y$ as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], and put $V_0=V\times_Y Y_0$. By [def-a1-space-open-subspace], $V_0$ is an open subscheme of $Y_0$. More generally $X\times_YV\to X$ is representable by open immersions: its test on a scheme $T\to X$ is exactly the test $T\times_YV\to T$ of $j$. For every affine open $W\subseteq Y_0$, its composite $W\to Y$ is etale by [lem-a1-space-open-chart-tests] and [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. The hypothesis therefore makes $V\times_YW$ quasi-compact. By the definition of a quasi-compact scheme morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $j_0:V_0\to Y_0$ is quasi-compact. Every open immersion is a monomorphism: two maps into the open with equal ambient maps have the same points and the same structure-sheaf maps. Its diagonal is consequently an isomorphism, hence a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion], and it is quasi-separated. This applies to $j_0$ and all its scheme base changes.

source.place: Tag 089D (lemma-flat-morphism-scheme-theoretically-dense-open), proof; Tags 0833 and 0836, etale-local interpretation of density.

proof.text: For any etale scheme chart $a:T\to X$, form $P=T\times_Y Y_0$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $P$ is a scheme and $q:P\to T$ is a surjective etale morphism. By [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], $a q:P\to X$ is etale. The scheme map $g:P\to Y_0$ is flat: the square with vertical etale maps $P\to X$ and $Y_0\to Y$ is one of the chart tests in the definition of flatness [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. This argument requires neither $f$ nor the atlases to be quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 089D (lemma-flat-morphism-scheme-theoretically-dense-open), proof; Tags 0833 and 0836, etale-local interpretation of density.

proof.text: Choose $T\to X$ in step 2 to be a surjective scheme atlas. Then $P\to X$ is a surjective etale scheme chart. Its pullback of $j_X$ is $V_0\times_{Y_0}P\to P$, which is quasi-compact by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change] applied to $j_0$. It is an open immersion by the scheme-test description in step 1, and its diagonal is an isomorphism, hence a closed immersion, as proved there. Apply [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local] to $j_X$ and the singleton target cover $P\to X$: every local map is both quasi-compact and separated, exactly the conjunction the cited statement requires. It follows that $j_X$ is quasi-compact (and separated). In particular its inverse image on every affine etale scheme chart of $X$ is quasi-compact, as required.

source.place: Tag 089D (lemma-flat-morphism-scheme-theoretically-dense-open), proof; Tags 0833 and 0836, etale-local interpretation of density.

proof.text: Restrict the assumed injection $\mathcal O_Y\to j_*\mathcal O_V$ to $Y_0$. The section formula and structure-sheaf restriction in [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction] identify it with $\mathcal O_{Y_0}\to(j_0)_*\mathcal O_{V_0}$ on the small etale site, hence also on all Zariski opens of $Y_0$. Its kernel is zero. Thus the largest quasi-coherent ideal contained in that kernel is zero, and [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] gives $\operatorname{SIm}(j_0)=Y_0$. For any chart $T\to X$ and the flat scheme map $g:P\to Y_0$ of step 2, apply [lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback] to $j_0$ and $g$. Its hypotheses hold: $j_0$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by step 1, and its scheme-theoretic image is $Y_0$. Therefore $k:V_0\times_{Y_0}P\to P$ has scheme-theoretic image $P$. The map $k$ is quasi-compact by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change]. Applying [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc] with this image equal to $P$ shows that $\Gamma(P,\mathcal O_P)\to\Gamma(V_0\times_{Y_0}P,\mathcal O)$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 089D (lemma-flat-morphism-scheme-theoretically-dense-open), proof; Tags 0833 and 0836, etale-local interpretation of density.

proof.text: To prove the desired sheaf injection, let $T\to X$ be any object of the small etale site and let $s\in\mathcal O_X(T)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ restrict to zero on $T\times_X(X\times_YV)$. Direct-image sections are the sections on this fibre product, by the same section description of [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction]. Pull back $s$ to the surjective etale cover $P=T\times_Y Y_0\to T$ of step 2. Fibre-product associativity identifies its restriction to $V_0\times_{Y_0}P$ with the pullback of the assumed zero restriction. Step 4 therefore gives $s|_P=0$. The uniqueness axiom for the structure sheaf on the etale cover $P\to T$ implies $s=0$. This proves injectivity on every object $T$ and hence injectivity of $\mathcal O_X\to(j_X)_*\mathcal O_{X\times_YV}$. Together with steps 1 and 3 this proves all clauses.

Step 4: the injection restricts to Y_0 by the pushforward-restriction node, so SIm(j_0)=Y_0. lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback (qcqs j_0, flat g) gives SIm(k)=P, and scheme-image-ideal-qc gives the injection on sections. Step 5: the sheaf axiom on the cover {P→T} gives injectivity on every étale T. Edge cases V=∅ and V=Y hold. I found no duplicate among the algebraic-space nodes on density and flatness.
